title: Interface-Controlled Spin-Orbit Torques in Rare-Earth Synthetic Ferrimagnets Probed by Sagnac Magneto-Optics and Harmonic Hall Measurements
authors: Akilan K, Koral Aykin, Jose-Luis Ampuero, Laurent Badie, Stephane Mangin, Sébastien Petit-Watelot, Michel Hehn, Andrew D. Kent, J. -Carlos Rojas-Sánchez
abstract: Spin-orbit torque (SOT) provides an efficient route for manipulating magnetization in spintronic devices, and its accurate quantification is essential. Here, we investigate Co/Gd-based synthetic ferrimagnets using complementary magnetotransport and magneto-optical techniques. We use a Sagnac magneto-optical interferometry method to directly quantify current-induced magnetization tilting and extract the damping-like SOT effective field. The Sagnac measurements show good agreement with harmonic Hall analysis across different Co/Gd and Gd/Pt/Co heterostructures, providing a quantitative determination of the damping-like SOT effective field that does not rely on electrical transport signatures. By varying the Gd thickness and multilayer stacking order, we demonstrate that the damping-like torque is strongly influenced by spin transport and angular momentum conversion at rare-earth and heavy-metal interfaces. The observation of a finite torque in Gd/Pt/Co/Pt structures, where conventional Pt spin Hall contributions are expected to compensate, highlights the active role of the Gd layer in SOT generation. Furthermore, interface engineering enables perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in Gd/Pt/Co/Al heterostructures with a 2-nm-thick Co layer, allowing current-induced SOT switching at current densities of 8-10 MA/cm$^2$. These results establish rare-earth-based synthetic ferrimagnets as a versatile platform for engineering spin-orbit phenomena and optimizing low-power spintronic devices.
summary: This work investigates Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT) in rare-earth synthetic ferrimagnets using a combination of Sagnac magneto-optics and harmonic Hall measurements. By comparing these techniques, the authors provide a robust, quantitative determination of the SOT effective field. The findings establish these rare-earth systems as excellent platforms for designing low-power spintronic devices through precise interface engineering.
main_problem: The paper aims to accurately quantify the Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT) in magnetic thin films, which is crucial for developing energy-efficient spintronic devices.
main_result: The study demonstrates that rare-earth-based synthetic ferrimagnets are a versatile platform for engineering SOT phenomena, achieving current-induced switching at low current densities via interface engineering.
method: The research employs complementary techniques, combining Sagnac magneto-optical interferometry with harmonic Hall measurements to independently and quantitatively determine the damping-like SOT effective field.
model_or_system: The physical system under investigation consists of Co/Gd-based synthetic ferrimagnets (SFiMs) and related heterostructures (e.g., Gd/Pt/Co/Al). The measurements probe the magnetization dynamics and torque generation at rare-earth/heavy-metal interfaces.
key_observables: Damping-like SOT effective field ($\xi_{DL}$), current-induced magnetization tilting (measured optically), and various Hall/Kerr resistances ($R_{2\omega}^{xy}$, $	heta_K$).
important_parameters: Current densities ($\ge 8-10 	ext{ MA/cm}^2$), Gd layer thickness, and multilayer stacking order.
main_assumptions: The harmonic Hall analysis requires careful correction for nonlinear magnon contributions, and initial analyses sometimes incorrectly assumed $	ext{M}_{	ext{eff}} \gg 	ext{H}_{\parallel}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate AHE vs. field measurements, magnetotransport data showing angular dependence, and Kerr rotation vs. current/field, demonstrating the dependence of anisotropy on device geometry.
paper_structure: The paper develops the need for accurate SOT quantification, compares Sagnac MOKE results against harmonic Hall analysis, details the influence of interface engineering (Gd layer) on torque generation, and concludes by showing successful SOT switching in engineered structures.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the precise measurement of torque and magnetization dynamics using optical methods (MOKE) and transport measurements provides fundamental insights into interfacial coupling and spin-charge conversion, which are relevant to open quantum systems modeling.
